transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess I’m here because something happened at work that maybe looked worse than I meant it to.

We were in a staff meeting, and I got kind of worked up talking about fall prevention, and I… sort of acted out a whole drill with the chairs and my arms going. I know that sounds odd. People were telling me to sit down, but I had a hard time stopping right away. I wasn’t trying to cause trouble or anything. It just kind of got away from me.
Before that meeting, had you been feeling unusually energized or “up” compared with your normal self?

Yeah… I mean, maybe a little more than usual. Not in a bad way, exactly. I felt kind of bright, like fired up, like things were finally making sense and lining up, you know?

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but when I’m like that and someone slows me down or questions what I’m saying, I can get… sharper than I mean to. I snap a bit, and then afterward I feel bad about it. Does that make sense?
During this time, have you been needing much less sleep than usual?

Um… yeah, I guess so. I don’t want to make it sound like I was trying to stay up all night or anything. It’s just, I’d sleep maybe two or three hours, then wake up before dawn and feel like I was ready to get going.

And at the time it didn’t feel strange to me. I’d be up while the house was still dark, making plans in my head or writing things down, and I kind of thought, well, I’m just being productive. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
During this time, have you been hearing or seeing things that other people couldn't?

Um… not seeing things, no. Hearing, maybe. I don’t want that to sound worse than it is.

Sometimes if I’m by myself, like in the hallway at work or at home near the laundry room, I’ll hear my name, or I’ll hear what sounds like a resident calling for help. It’s clear enough that I go check, because it sounds real. But then there’s nobody there.

It doesn’t happen constantly or anything. I just… I guess it has happened enough that I noticed it. Is that what you mean?
When you heard your name or a resident calling, was that only during the same time you were feeling especially energized and sleeping very little?

Not only then, I don’t think. I mean, it was more noticeable when I was all wound up and not sleeping, sure.

But there was also a calmer stretch after that, where I was sleeping more normal and I wasn’t running around with all these projects, and it still happened for a few weeks. I’d hear my name called sometimes.

And… I guess I was still pretty sure people at work were keeping notes on me. I know that sounds kind of suspicious, and I’m not trying to be difficult. It just felt real to me at the time. Is that helpful to say?
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in almost everything most of the day, nearly every day?

Um… I don’t know if I’d call it depressed like that. I mean, I’ve had down days, sure, where I don’t feel like doing much, but I’m not sure about two whole weeks most of the day, every day.

I don’t want to say no if I’m forgetting something, but… nothing really stands out to me that way. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you were hearing things or felt people were keeping notes on you, but you were not feeling unusually energized or up during that time?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it was, but there was a calmer stretch after I wasn’t so wound up anymore.

I was sleeping more normal, and I wasn’t rushing around doing all those projects or feeling all keyed up. But for a few weeks after that, I still heard my name being called sometimes. And I still felt pretty sure people at work were keeping notes on me.

I know that probably sounds… not great. But that is how it felt then. Does that answer what you mean?
During that energized period, were you hospitalized because of your behavior?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t think I have a clear thing to point to there.

I mean, I know things got… intense during that time, but whether I was actually hospitalized because of my behavior, I’d have to think about what you mean by hospitalized. I don’t want to say the wrong thing.
During that energized period, did your behavior cause serious problems at work or at home?

Yeah… I guess it did, more than I wanted to admit.

At work, the senior center ended up putting me on leave. I don’t like saying that, because I don’t want it to sound like I was trying to cause problems or anything. And at home, my wife’s had to remind me more about chores and appointments because I’m just not keeping up the way I used to.

I’ve also kind of pulled back from people at church. And I worry now about whether I can safely go back to caregiving work. So… yes, I think it caused problems. Is that what you mean?
During that energized period, did you believe people at work were keeping notes on you?

Yeah… during the fired-up times, I did think that.

I was only sleeping a few hours and making all these big plans, and I started feeling pretty sure my supervisor was watching for mistakes or setting little traps for me. Like people were writing things down about me at work.

I know that may sound paranoid, and I’m not trying to make excuses, but at the time it felt real. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
During that energized period, did you hear your name or a resident calling for help?

Yeah… I mean, not all the time, but that did happen.

Sometimes if I was by myself in the hallway, or even at home near the laundry room, I’d hear my name. Or I’d hear what sounded like a resident calling for help, clear as day. And I’d go check, because I didn’t want to ignore somebody if they needed me… but then there wouldn’t be anyone there.

I know that probably sounds bad. I’m not trying to make it into something bigger than it is, but yes, that happened. Is that what you mean?
Before this recent episode, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt unusually energized or up for several days in a row?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I didn’t always see it as a problem at the time.

There have been stretches before where I felt really bright, like fired up, like everything was finally lining up and I could handle things better than usual. It would go on for several days, not just a good mood for an afternoon.

But… if somebody slowed me down or questioned what I was doing, I’d get irritated fast. I’d snap harder than I meant to. I don’t like admitting that part, because I’m not trying to be a harsh person. But yes, I think I’ve had times like that before. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During one of those energized periods, did it ever last a full week or longer?

Yeah… I think it did. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, because some days were stronger than others, but it wasn’t just a day or two.

Those stretches where I was too energized, hardly sleeping, and pushing big plans… they’ve kind of been coming and going for maybe around 11 months now. And some of those periods, yes, they lasted a week or longer.

Does that make sense the way I’m saying it?
Have you ever had a time lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m not sure… I mean, I’ve had low days, definitely. Times where I didn’t feel like myself or I felt worn down.

But a solid two weeks where I was depressed most of the day nearly every day… I don’t know if I can say that for sure. I wouldn’t want to say yes if I’m not remembering it right.

What counts as “depressed” in the way you mean it?
